subject: Mathematics
name: Mathematics, Year 7
syllabus: Victorian Curriculum F-10 Version 2.0: Mathematics, Level 7

points.title: Square numbers and square roots
points.brief: A square number is a whole number multiplied by itself, such as 7 × 7 = 49. The square root undoes squaring, so √49 = 7.

points.title: Expanded notation with powers of 10
points.brief: Writing a number by its place values as powers of ten, such as 4,305 = 4 × 10³ + 3 × 10² + 5.

points.title: Prime factorisation with indices
points.brief: Breaking a number into prime factors with a factor tree, then writing repeated factors with indices, such as 72 = 2³ × 3².

points.title: Fractions and decimals on a number line
points.brief: Placing positive and negative fractions, decimals and mixed numbers on a number line, using equivalent forms to compare them.

points.title: Adding and subtracting fractions
points.brief: Rewrite fractions with a common denominator, then add or subtract the numerators, such as 2/3 + 1/4 = 8/12 + 3/12 = 11/12.

points.title: Multiplying fractions
points.brief: Multiply the numerators and the denominators, changing mixed numbers to improper fractions first and simplifying at the end.

points.title: Dividing fractions
points.brief: To divide by a fraction, multiply by its reciprocal, such as 3/4 ÷ 1/2 = 3/4 × 2/1 = 3/2.

points.title: Rounding decimals and estimating
points.brief: Rounding to a given number of decimal places, and rounding before calculating to check an answer is reasonable.

points.title: Multiplying and dividing decimals
points.brief: Multiply as whole numbers and count the decimal places. To divide by a decimal, move the point the same way in both numbers first.

points.title: Finding a percentage of a quantity
points.brief: Change the percentage to a decimal or fraction and multiply, such as 15% of 60 = 0.15 × 60 = 9.

points.title: Writing one quantity as a percentage of another
points.brief: Divide the part by the whole and multiply by 100, using the same units for both, such as 18 out of 24 is 75%.

points.title: Adding and subtracting integers
points.brief: Ordering integers on a number line, and adding and subtracting them, where subtracting a negative number is the same as adding.

points.title: Simplifying ratios
points.brief: A ratio compares parts of the same kind. Divide each part by their highest common factor, such as 12:18 = 2:3.

points.title: Dividing a quantity in a ratio
points.brief: Add the parts to find the total number of shares, find one share, then multiply, such as $60 in the ratio 2:3 gives $24 and $36.

points.title: Best buys with unit prices
points.brief: Compare products of different sizes by working out the price for one unit, such as cents per 100 g, and picking the lowest.

points.title: Variables and substitution
points.brief: A letter stands for a number that can change. Substitute values into a formula, such as P = 2l + 2w, to find the unknown.

points.title: Writing algebraic expressions
points.brief: Turning words into algebra, such as 5 more than 3 times n is 3n + 5, and the conventions that 3n means 3 × n.

points.title: The laws of arithmetic
points.brief: The commutative, associative and distributive laws let you regroup a calculation, such as 7 × 98 = 7 × 100 - 7 × 2.

points.title: Solving one-variable equations
points.brief: Use inverse operations to undo each step and find the unknown, such as 3x + 5 = 20 gives x = 5, then check by substituting.

points.title: The Cartesian plane
points.brief: Plotting points as (x, y) in all four quadrants, reading across first and then up or down.

points.title: Tables of values from a rule
points.brief: Substitute x values into a rule such as y = 2x + 1 to fill a table, then plot the pairs to see the pattern.

points.title: Finding the rule for a pattern
points.brief: For a growing pattern, such as squares made of matchsticks, find how much it grows each step and write a rule for the nth term.

points.title: Reading graphs of real data
points.brief: What rising, flat and falling parts of a graph mean, such as a travel graph where a flat part shows a stop.

points.title: Area of rectangles and triangles
points.brief: A rectangle's area is length times width. A triangle's is half the base times the perpendicular height.

points.title: Area of a parallelogram
points.brief: Cutting a triangle off one end and moving it to the other makes a rectangle, so a parallelogram's area is base times perpendicular height.

points.title: Volume of rectangular prisms
points.brief: Volume is length times width times height, measured in cubic units such as cm³.

points.title: Volume of triangular prisms
points.brief: The volume of any right prism is the area of its cross-section times its length, so a triangular prism is ½ × b × h × length.

points.title: Pi and the parts of a circle
points.brief: Radius, diameter and circumference, and why the circumference divided by the diameter is always pi, about 3.14.

points.title: Angles on parallel lines
points.brief: When a transversal crosses parallel lines, corresponding angles are equal, alternate angles are equal, and co-interior angles add to 180°.

points.title: Angle sum of a triangle
points.brief: The three angles of a triangle add to 180°, so the third angle is 180° minus the other two.

points.title: Angle sum of a polygon
points.brief: A polygon with n sides splits into n - 2 triangles, so its angles add to (n - 2) × 180°.

points.title: Drawing 3D objects in two dimensions
points.brief: Nets, isometric drawings, and the front, side and top views of an object, and what each shows or hides.

points.title: Classifying triangles
points.brief: Triangles named by their sides (equilateral, isosceles, scalene) and by their angles (acute, right, obtuse).

points.title: Classifying quadrilaterals
points.brief: The side, angle and diagonal properties of squares, rectangles, rhombuses, parallelograms, trapeziums and kites, and how they relate.

points.title: Transformations on the Cartesian plane
points.brief: How translations, reflections in an axis and rotations about the origin change coordinates, such as reflecting in the x-axis changes the sign of y.

points.title: Types of data
points.brief: Categorical data names groups. Numerical data is counted (discrete) or measured (continuous).

points.title: Mean, median, mode and range
points.brief: The mean is the total divided by the count, the median the middle value in order, the mode the most common, and the range the highest minus the lowest.

points.title: Choosing a measure of centre
points.brief: An outlier pulls the mean towards it but barely moves the median, so the median often suits data with extreme values.

points.title: Dot plots and stem-and-leaf plots
points.brief: Reading and making dot plots and stem-and-leaf plots, and finding the median and range from them.

points.title: Describing a distribution
points.brief: Describing data by its shape, centre and spread, and pointing out clusters, gaps and outliers.

points.title: Sample spaces
points.brief: The sample space is the list of every possible outcome of an experiment, such as {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6} for a die.

points.title: Probability of a single event
points.brief: With equally likely outcomes, probability is favourable outcomes over total outcomes, a number from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).

points.title: Expected number of results
points.brief: Multiply the probability by the number of trials to predict how often an outcome should happen, such as 60 rolls giving about 10 sixes.

points.title: Relative frequency and the number of trials
points.brief: Relative frequency is how often an outcome happened over the number of trials. More trials usually bring it closer to the theoretical probability.
